build: current working tree with pre-existing uncommitted changes; Vite :4015 and controller :8080

findings.title: Keyboard focus disappears on the theme selector
findings.confidence: Confirmed by keyboard and computed styles
findings.observation: Help → Tab from the deployment warning to Dashboard color theme. The selector is focused and matches :focus-visible, but its computed outline style is none and box-shadow is none. Its border retains the normal low-emphasis border. This affects the shared header across the application.
findings.recommendation: ThemeToggle sets outline: none inline, overriding the shared focus-visible rule. Remove that override and give the closed control a clearly visible theme-token focus treatment. Preserve a visible focus indicator inside the open menu as well.

findings.title: Solarized Light warning text is too faint
findings.observation: Monitoring’s DEGRADED badge uses 11px text in rgb(181,137,0). Its orange translucent fill over the cream card produces an estimated contrast of 2.39:1 using the computed ancestor backgrounds. This is below the 4.5:1 benchmark for normal text. The warning is harder to read precisely when it needs attention.
findings.recommendation: Use the semantic warning text/background/border tokens as a matched set instead of using the decorative --warning color as text on a hard-coded orange fill. Check danger, success and info badges across all five themes too; the 2.39:1 measurement applies to this specific badge, not every status.

findings.title: Checkboxes use two different color systems
findings.confidence: Confirmed in rendered controls and DOM styles
findings.observation: Controller & runtime’s Desktop Client Promotion and Client Software Downloads controls have accent-color: auto. Show queued runs in Schedules also keeps the native checked appearance. In Solarized Light the checked box is browser blue despite the olive application accent; in Monokai it remains a native pale check despite the pink accent. Repository checkboxes, by comparison, explicitly compute to the violet theme accent in Dark. Runtime checkboxes are about 13 CSS px, with nearly no gap before Enabled/Disabled.
findings.recommendation: Give native checkboxes and radios a shared baseline using --accent, consistent dimensions, label spacing, disabled styling and focus behavior. Retain native semantics; a custom replacement is unnecessary just to fix accent color. Preserve explicit destructive-checkbox exceptions.

findings.title: Governance Audit dates fall back to bare browser inputs
findings.observation: The From and Until date-time fields are approximately 20.9 CSS px high, white in both Light and Solarized Light and rgb(59,59,59) in Dark. They sit directly against inline labels beside a much larger themed Project scope selector. The surrounding text filters use .settings-input; the date inputs do not. Results Library and the booking dialog already show substantially better themed date-field treatments.
findings.recommendation: Route date/time inputs through the shared form-field styling: tokenized surface, text, border, radius, spacing, focus and disabled states. Keep native date editing and picker behavior unless a documented product requirement justifies replacing it. Align labels above the controls.

findings.title: Hover help has multiple implementations
findings.observation: The inspected sidebar and editor attach help through native HTML title attributes. Those popup tooltips belong to the browser/OS and do not inherit the application palette. Elsewhere, source mapping supplies a CSS data-tooltip bubble and charts use a separate tokenized Recharts tooltip helper. The source-mapping chips also retain title, so two help mechanisms can coexist on a single trigger. Screenshots identify the affected surfaces but do not prove the appearance or timing of a native popup.
findings.recommendation: Use one application tooltip component for short help with a themed opaque surface, keyboard focus support, an accessible description, Escape dismissal and edge collision handling. Remove redundant title only when equivalent accessible help exists. Keep critical instructions and disabled-action reasons visible or available through a persistent help control.

findings.title: Settings focus rings retain the default indigo hue
findings.confidence: Confirmed by keyboard and computed styles
findings.observation: With Monokai selected, focusing Max Concurrent Tests yields the correct pink border but a fixed rgba(99,102,241,0.18) outer shadow. The same CSS governs text and select fields. Other source styles also contain fixed blue/indigo emphasis. These are separate from the correctly changing theme tokens.
findings.recommendation: Replace the hard-coded ring with --focus-ring or a derived accent token and standardize focus thickness and offset. Audit focus and selection independently of resting colors; a screen can look themed while its interactive states are not.

findings.title: Scheduling links escape the selected palette
findings.observation: In Monokai, Schedule defaults and Capacity commitments and standing allocations inside Scheduled bookings appear as lavender browser-style links. The same destination links above the calendar use pink themed button styling. One screen therefore presents equivalent navigation in visibly different color systems.
findings.recommendation: Provide a shared text-link treatment with theme-aware default, visited, hover and focus states. Use it for inline navigation; reserve button styling for the action hierarchy the product intends. Do not rely on the browser’s visited-link palette.

findings.title: Field labels and control density vary within the same form
findings.observation: Script Library mixes uppercase compact labels (Search scripts, Run release, Folder) with larger sentence-case labels (Assigned application/release). New Test mixes compact uppercase filter labels with larger inline Sort scenarios and Launch application labels. Governance combines placeholder-only text filters with inline date labels. These variations make neighboring controls look as though they come from different products.
findings.recommendation: Define a small set of deliberate field sizes and one label/hint/error pattern. Apply those patterns within each form and filter toolbar. Give important filters persistent visible labels; aria-label alone does not preserve visual context after typing. Avoid making every control globally the same size regardless of context.

findings.title: A disabled scenario choice can look selected on hover
findings.observation: The disabled Copy Existing Scenario card can receive the same accent border/fill as the selected New Scenario card when hovered. Both cards are accent-filled in the captured state, even though the copy path is disabled because the workspace has no saved scenarios. The selector .scenario-source-card:hover does not exclude disabled controls.
findings.recommendation: Restrict hover styling to enabled controls and give disabled choices a distinct, readable treatment. Keep the explanation visible and preserve an unambiguous selected state. Test hover, keyboard focus, selected and disabled combinations together.

findings.title: Report errors leave loading copy and no local recovery action
findings.confidence: Confirmed in the available archive; data-dependent
findings.observation: Opening DOC-RUN-20260612-002 displayed Controller reported a server error, six n/a KPI cards, and Findings will appear when the report loads. The visible Summary surface offers no retry next to the error. This mixes a terminal error message with a loading expectation and leaves the user without a clear recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Use a shared error state with a specific explanation, a Retry action and a route back to results. Replace loading-oriented copy when the load has failed. This finding concerns error presentation; the underlying server failure was not diagnosed in this design audit.

findings.title: Navigation families and empty-state guidance vary
findings.observation: The app uses filled segmented navigation in the header, underlined result tabs, pill filters in libraries, vertical runtime category buttons, and compact administrative links. These can serve different purposes, but equivalent selection states and sizes are not consistently expressed. Command Center gives an actionable empty state; Results Library tells users to run or pull a result without a matching action in that empty-state panel. Empty Script Library still shows a large filter and table scaffold.
findings.recommendation: Assign clear roles to page navigation, view tabs, filters and workflow steps, then standardize each family. Keep primary next actions adjacent to empty-state explanations and reduce irrelevant filter/table scaffolding when a workspace has never contained data.

findings.title: Existing checks do not guard these specific visual states
findings.confidence: Source review; tests not executed for this audit
findings.observation: The repository already has theme token tests, select styling tests, theme coverage for Help, and a workflow that visits major routes across five themes and two widths. The reviewed workflow-ux-consistency test checks route headings, theme attributes, toolbar structure and visibility, then saves screenshots. It does not compare those screenshots to expected images or assert the checkbox accent, bare date-field style, closed theme-selector focus ring or this warning badge contrast.
findings.recommendation: Extend the existing suite with a representative control matrix and focused browser assertions, rather than adding another route-only smoke test. Cover checked/unchecked/indeterminate/disabled controls; empty/filled/invalid text and date fields; select open/closed; native fallback; tooltip hover/focus; and high-risk status contrast. Run the affected flows in dev-admin and local-auth profiles when implementing changes.

steps.title: Dashboard and shared shell
steps.notes: Persistent navigation, a clear primary New Test entry point, and consistent overall surfaces. Narrow capture is from the running packaged frontend on :8080; subsequent work uses the current workspace frontend on :4015. This is not evidence that those two builds are identical.
